correctness.rationale: For the standard polar of cube plus cross-polytope, chambers with sorted positive coordinates map triangularly to a standard Dirichlet simplex, with 2^d d! congruent chambers. This yields volume 2^d/(d+1)!, covariance v_d I with v_d=[2(d+1)-H_(d+1)^2-H_(d+1)^(2)]/[d(d+1)(d+2)], and L=[(d+1)!]^(1/d)*sqrt(v_d)/2. The cross-polytope ratio obeys R_d^2=(d+1)^(2/d)*(1-c_(d+1)/(2d)), c_m=H_m^2+H_m^(2)-2. Fresh exact rational checks verify all 150 dimension-by-dimension independent Dirichlet moment formulas and comparisons d=2..25 (the proof only needs d=2..18). At m=20 the exact base inequality c_m>4log m and the positive increment for m>=6 prove strictness for d>=19, with equality d=1. Harmonic-number asymptotics imply 1-R_d~(log d)^2/(4d); numerical scaled ratios at d=100,1000,10000 corroborate but do not prove the limit. A separate d=2 polygon computation has area 2/3, covariance coordinate 23/432. Normalizations are for uniform volume, not vertices.

value.rationale: The canonical signohedron is an independently studied symmetric polytope family; its affine-invariant isotropic constant is a natural interior measure invariant. The exact all-dimensional harmonic formula and strict, sharp asymptotic gap relative to the cross-polytope are nontrivial, not determined by the previously classified face/vertex/radius data. Future work on isotropic optimization of explicit polar Minkowski sums could use this benchmark; the claim does not assert global extremality.

limitations: Coordinate covariance holds for the fixed standard representative; isotropic L is affine invariant.
